text: A Grothendieck topos is a category equivalent to the category of sheaves $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal{C},J)$ on a ___.
explanation: The chapter defines a Grothendieck topos as a category equivalent to $\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal{C},J)$, the sheaves on a site: a category $\mathcal{C}$ equipped with a Grothendieck topology $J$. A bare topological space is only the special case $\mathcal{O}(X)$; the general definition requires a site.
